# QS-CFW-6160-72 - Quality specification - crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (4340)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-6160-72

## Scope
This quality specification defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 supplied by the P1 forging cell. The document applies to the forged blank state of material grade 4340 intended for downstream machining and heat treatment. It provides background rationale for the selected characteristics, inspection method details for verification, recordkeeping requirements, and examples of disposition outcomes.

## Background and rationale
The crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 is produced for high-stress rotating applications and must meet metallurgical and dimensional characteristics that enable predictable heat treatment and machining yield. Mechanical hardness in the forged condition correlates to prior thermal processing and cooling rate; maintaining the specified hardness range ensures the material will respond to downstream heat treatment as expected. Bore accuracy is critical for fit-up and concentricity during machining operations; the specified tolerance supports effective fixture alignment. Maximum forging weight is a manufacturing constraint driven by die strength and press capacity and is included to prevent equipment overload and to ensure handling safety.

The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26-31 HRC. The bore diameter tolerance for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is ±0.09 mm. The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26.9 kg.

## Requirements table
| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance criteria |
|---|---:|---|
| Material grade | 4340 | Visual and mill certification match part drawing and purchase order. |
| Hardness (forged blank) | 26-31 HRC | Hardness readings within specified range across verified locations. |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.09 mm | Bore measured relative to nominal drawing diameter and within tolerance. |
| Forging weight | ≤ 26.9 kg | Measured mass does not exceed maximum forging weight. |
| Surface condition | No forging laps, cold shuts, or scale beyond normal mill scale | Defects affecting machinability or fatigue rejection per visual acceptance; see inspection method. |
| Heat treatment traceability | Batch heat history documented | Records retained per inspection method. |

Notes:
- The hardness and bore tolerance items are mandatory release criteria. Parts failing these criteria shall be held and processed according to nonconformance handling.
- Maximum forging weight is a production limit; parts produced above this value shall be segregated and dispositioned.

## Inspection method
Overview: Inspection shall consist of documented sampling and 100% checks where specified by downstream needs. Visual inspection, dimensional measurement, hardness testing, and weight verification are the primary activities. All inspections shall be logged on the work order and retained as the quality record.

1. Visual inspection
- Perform a visual examination of the forged blank for laps, cold shuts, cracks, and excessive scale. Use lighting suitable for detection of surface anomalies and compare to the acceptance criteria noted in the requirements table.
- Examples: a shallow surface seam that can be removed in machining without losing effective section may be acceptable; a through-thickness crack is not acceptable.

2. Dimensional inspection - bore
- Verify the bore diameter using a bore gauge, plug gauge, or equivalent calibrated instrument able to resolve the tolerances required for fit-up. Measurement points should include bore entry, mid-length, and exit where geometry allows.
- Record measurements on the inspection checklist and confirm each measured value lies within the bore diameter tolerance of ±0.09 mm from nominal.

3. Hardness testing
- Conduct hardness testing on the forged blank at specified locations representative of the core forging cross-sections. Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester appropriate for HRC scale and follow manufacturer procedures for indenter and load.
- Ensure surfaces are prepared to allow a valid indenter reading. Record individual readings and the location for traceability. The hardness range for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26-31 HRC; acceptance requires all recorded readings to fall within this range.

4. Weight verification
- Weigh the forged blank using a calibrated scale and capture the value on the inspection record. The maximum forging weight for crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 (CFW-6160-72) is 26.9 kg; blanks exceeding that value must be segregated and flagged for disposition.

5. Recording and traceability
- Retain the following records with the batch lot file: material certification, hardness readings with location notations, bore measurement records, weight record, and visual inspection checklist. Records shall accompany material through shipping and be available to Quality on request.

## Nonconformance handling
When a blank fails to meet any requirement in the requirements table, follow this procedure:

- Segregation: Immediately segregate the nonconforming blank and tag with a nonconformance tag indicating the nature of the failure (hardness, bore, weight, surface defect). Maintain physical and administrative control to prevent inadvertent use.
- Notification: Notify the plant quality engineer and production supervisor. Provide the inspection records that document the nonconformance.
- Evaluation and disposition: The quality engineer shall evaluate the nonconformance against downstream process capability and part function. Disposition options include:
  - Rework: If the defect is remediable by machining or minor corrective action without compromising material properties, the blank may be reworked to drawing requirements. Document the rework plan and re-inspect critical characteristics. Example: a localized surface seam that can be removed by machining without reducing required section or altering balance.
  - Scrap: If the defect cannot be corrected without compromising integrity or if the forging weight exceeds limits in a way that prevents safe handling, scrap the part. Document the reason for scrapping and retain photos and inspection records.
  - Return to supplier or remelt: If a systematic forging/process issue is suspected, hold affected lot items and initiate containment plus root cause analysis.

- Records: For every nonconformance, retain the original inspection report, photos (if applicable), disposition form, and evidence of re-inspection or scrap. These records form the corrective action evidence and are kept with the batch file.

- Root cause and corrective action: For repeated or systemic failures, the quality engineer shall lead a root cause analysis, define corrective actions, and track effectiveness. Document the analysis and corrective actions in the lot file and reference in future production reviews.

## Examples and practical notes
- Example 1: A blank records hardness readings within range except one location reading below the specified range. Segregate and evaluate whether the low reading is localized and machinable; disposition by re-inspection after additional hardness testing along adjacent locations.
- Example 2: A bore measurement at one end is outside the tolerance of ±0.09 mm while other points are acceptable. Determine if the deviation affects fixture fit-up; if so, hold and disposition per corrective action.

Quality retention: All inspection and disposition records shall be maintained with the lot documentation for the lifetime required by customer contract. This specification is the controlling acceptance standard for the crankshaft blank CFW-6160-72 at plant P1.
